title: Rice Husk Briquette Production
description: Convert rice husks into high-energy briquettes for cooking fuel and heating applications. This process helps reduce waste while creating valuable fuel products.
steps: Collect and dry rice husks in the sun for 2-3 days until moisture content is below 15%
Mix rice husks with binding agent (clay soil or cassava starch) in ratio 10:1
Add small amount of water to form moldable paste consistency
Use briquette press or manual mold to shape into uniform blocks
Dry briquettes in shade for 24-48 hours until completely hardened
Test burn quality - good briquettes should burn steadily with minimal smoke
Package in waterproof containers for storage and sale
materials_needed: Clay soil or cassava starch (1 kg)

title: Vegetable Waste Composting
description: Transform vegetable trimmings and kitchen scraps into nutrient-rich compost for organic farming and soil improvement.
steps: Collect vegetable peels, leaves, and non-meat kitchen scraps daily
Chop large pieces into smaller 2-3 inch segments for faster decomposition
Create compost pile in shaded area with good drainage
Layer green waste (vegetable scraps) with brown materials (dry leaves, paper)
Maintain 3:1 brown to green ratio for optimal decomposition
Turn pile weekly with pitchfork to ensure proper aeration
Keep moisture level like wrung-out sponge - add water if too dry
Monitor temperature - should heat up to 130-160°F in center
Compost ready in 2-3 months when dark, crumbly, and earthy-smelling
materials_needed: Dry leaves, straw, or shredded paper
Wire mesh or wooden pallets for bin construction

title: Bagasse Paper Pulp Production
description: Process sugarcane bagasse into paper pulp for manufacturing eco-friendly paper products and packaging materials.
steps: Collect fresh bagasse immediately after juice extraction to prevent fermentation
Remove any remaining sugar by washing bagasse thoroughly with clean water
Chop bagasse into uniform 1-2 inch pieces using mechanical chopper
Soak chopped bagasse in water for 24 hours to soften fibers
Boil bagasse in large pot with 2% sodium hydroxide solution for 3-4 hours
Rinse thoroughly until water runs clear to remove chemicals
Beat pulp mechanically or manually until fibers separate completely
Screen pulp through fine mesh to remove impurities and lumps
Press pulp to remove excess water and form sheets
Air dry pulp sheets for 24-48 hours before packaging

title: Fruit Seed Oil Extraction
description: Extract valuable oils from fruit seeds for cosmetic, culinary, and industrial applications using mechanical pressing methods.
steps: Collect seeds from fresh fruits, removing all pulp and flesh completely
Wash seeds thoroughly and dry in sun for 5-7 days until completely moisture-free
Crack hard seed shells using hammer or mechanical cracker for enclosed seeds
Roast seeds lightly at 60°C for 30 minutes to improve oil yield
Grind roasted seeds into fine paste using oil expeller or heavy-duty grinder
Apply pressure using mechanical press or traditional methods to extract oil
Filter extracted oil through clean cloth to remove seed particles
Allow oil to settle for 24 hours, then decant clear oil from sediment
Store oil in dark glass bottles away from heat and sunlight
Test oil quality and document yield rates for business planning
materials_needed: Fresh fruit seeds (5-10 kg depending on variety)
Seed crackers or hammer for hard shells

title: Biochar Production from Mixed Agricultural Waste
description: Create biochar from various agricultural wastes through controlled pyrolysis for soil enhancement and carbon sequestration.
steps: Collect diverse agricultural waste: crop residues, pruned branches, husks, and shells
Dry all materials thoroughly to reduce moisture content below 20%
Size all materials uniformly - chop to 2-4 inch pieces
Build simple pyrolysis kiln using metal drums with controlled air inlet
Fill kiln with prepared waste materials, leaving space for air circulation
Start controlled burn with small amount of kindling at bottom
Maintain temperature between 300-500°C for 2-4 hours
Monitor smoke color - white smoke indicates water evaporation, blue smoke shows pyrolysis
Seal air inlets when smoke turns yellow to prevent complete combustion
Allow kiln to cool completely before opening (12-24 hours)
Crush biochar to desired size and test pH levels
Mix with compost or apply directly to soil as amendment
materials_needed: Metal drums or kiln construction materials

title: Rice Husk Animal Feed Preparation
description: Process rice husks into nutritious animal feed supplement through fermentation and mixing with protein sources.
steps: Collect fresh rice husks and remove any stones or foreign materials
Steam rice husks for 30 minutes to soften and sterilize
Cool steamed husks to room temperature in clean environment
Mix with molasses (5% by weight) to improve palatability
Add protein supplement like fish meal or soybean meal (10% by weight)
Inoculate with beneficial bacteria (EM or similar probiotics)
Ferment mixture in sealed containers for 7-14 days
Turn mixture every 2-3 days to ensure even fermentation
Test pH levels - should be between 3.8-4.2 when ready
Dry fermented feed to 12-15% moisture content for storage
Package in breathable bags and store in cool, dry place

title: Liquid Fertilizer from Vegetable Waste
description: Create nutrient-rich liquid fertilizer through anaerobic fermentation of vegetable trimmings and organic matter.
steps: Collect fresh vegetable trimmings, avoiding diseased or rotten materials
Chop all materials into small pieces (1 inch or smaller)
Fill large container 1/3 with chopped vegetable waste
Add brown sugar or jaggery (10% of waste weight) to accelerate fermentation
Pour clean water until container is 80% full, leaving space for gas expansion
Cover tightly with lid and seal all air gaps completely
Store in shaded area at ambient temperature (25-35°C optimal)
Allow fermentation for 3-4 weeks, releasing gas pressure weekly
Strain liquid through fine mesh when fermentation is complete
Dilute concentrated fertilizer 1:10 with water before application
Apply to plants during early morning or late evening
materials_needed: Large fermentation container with tight lid
